mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hp1404 enters S. aureus and accumulates in the cytoplasm at low concentration; this supports cell penetration rather than immediate classical membrane lysis.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The intracellular target is not identified in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: At low MIC concentration the paper reports no membrane lysis by TEM/SYTOX, while high concentration causes cytoplasmic structures and cell lysis; mechanism is concentration-dependent.
mechanism_claims.limitations: High-concentration membrane/cell-envelope damage should not be generalized to low-MIC killing.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LTA/LPS competition did not change the MIC against S. aureus, so LTA/LPS binding is not supported as the primary action site in this paper.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper discusses unpublished biolayer-interferometry data as data not shown; this final claim relies only on the reported competition assay and discussion.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Fifteen serial passages at sub-MIC Hp1404 did not increase MIC, unlike kanamycin; resistance-development result is linked to the proposed complex mechanism but is not itself a target-identification assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports robustness/no observed resistance in the assay, not a molecular target.
